issues.body: The matrix includes `macos-15` and `macos-15-intel`, but the new unconditional bash step runs `sha256sum -- "${archives[@]}"`. macOS ships `shasum` rather than GNU `sha256sum` by default. Both macOS matrix rows will therefore fail in archive mode, preventing their digest artifacts from being uploaded; because the collector needs the entire build matrix, the release and provenance jobs will never run successfully. The structural Python test does not execute this cross-platform command and therefore does not catch the failure.
issues.fix_hint: Use a portable digest implementation, for example select `shasum -a 256` on macOS and `sha256sum` elsewhere while preserving the exact `<64-hex>  <basename>` subject format, or compute the records with a small Python stdlib script available on all matrix runners. Add a hermetic test that exercises or structurally enforces the portable branch for the macOS matrix rows.
issues.title: Archive digest generation uses unavailable `sha256sum` on macOS runners

verdict.summary: The isolation contract test passes, but the release workflow is not portable across its own build matrix. The new digest step invokes GNU `sha256sum` on every archive runner, including the macOS tiers, where that command is not provided by the standard runner toolchain. Consequently the `package` reusable workflow will fail before producing the combined subjects, so the trusted-builder lane cannot complete on a real release.
